body.x: Anticipating high expectations in global entrance, Korean SMEs' products received rave reviews from the world's largest IT electronics exhibition CES 2015.

Daegu Technopark (Daegu TP) at the Mobile Technology Convergence Center (MTCC) opened a special hall for 23 mobile/IT start-up companies under the national policy "Global Competitiveness Strengthening Project for Mobile Convergence Industry," and announced it closed deals worth US$1.9 million through 1,292 consultations worth US$715 million at CES 2015, which was held at the Las Vegas Convention Center (LVCC) from Jan. 6-9.

One of the most noticeable companies among the exhibitors was Clips Tech, a manufacturer of Bluetooth wearable devices which introduced its Bluetooth headset "NeckBand" at CES. It sold 50,000 pieces on site, closing US$1.25 million with KW International of the U.S. It is planning to sell 20,000 more pieces to Amazon and a distributor in South America.

Also, UzBrainNet received loads of attention from decision makers from the major companies from around the world with its FPS (First Person Shooter) game enhancer "Rail-Gun" and ring-style wearable device "MotionRing." Nolla Design received US$70,000, the highest amount of fund which one can receive from the U.S. crowdfunding platform Kickstarter with its 5-watt solar charger, "Solarade."

A spokesperson from Daegu TP said, "With participation in GSMA Mobile World Congress in March and Hong Kong-China Sourcing Fair in April, we are going to continue supporting these mobile/IT SMEs to help them enter the global market."

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.

Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot. This year, AVING News is using smartphones for news reporting, in line with the trend of one-person media.
